newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Asia Commercial extends approval date.
newsitem.headline: Asia Commercial extends approval date.

text.p: Asia Commercial Holdings Ltd has extended the time for banks and noteholders of convertible notes to approve its capital and debt restructuring agreement, the company said in an announcement.

The chief reason for the extension is that one of the 14 banks involved has not yet signed the bank compromise agreement, the notice said. The agreement was to have been signed by all parties by January 10.

Asia Commercial said in the notice that it expected the remaining bank to sign the agreement by Wednesday, January 22, and has issued a revised timetable for the capital and debt restructuring proposals.

Under the restructuring proposal, Pacific Apex International Ltd, Leung Chung-Ping and Galmare Investment Ltd had agreed to subscribe for a total of 112.5 million shares of HK$1.00 each, representing about 40.2 percent of the restructured share capital of the company.

The latest time for signing of the bank compromise agreement is January 22 and the closing of the acceptance period for the offer in respect of the note exchange is 12 noon, Thursday, January 23 Geneva time from the previously published date of January 14, the notice.
The record date of the terms of the offer will be changed to January 28, 1997 from January 21.
The date for posting of the prospectus and application forms in relation to the subscription offer will be postponed to Wednesday, January 29.
The latest time for acceptance and payment of the offer will be Thursday, February 13, and the despatch of certificates for new shares and refund cheques on or about February 18, the notice said.
Dealing in Asia Commercial shares has been suspended since May 20, 1996 pending an agreement.
